60.text:

Reason : Bats and whales have four-chambered heart.

If both Assertion and Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion

2830.text: Which pair among the following does not have the same bond order?
2830.sol: We know that, For $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}$ Molecular orbital configuration of $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}$ is $\sigma \mathrm{l} s^2 \sigma^* 1 s^2 \sigma 2 s^2 \sigma^* 2 s^2 \sigma 2 p_z^2 \pi 2 p_x^2 \approx \pi 2 p_y^2 \pi^* 2 p_x^1$ Number of electrons in bonding orbital $=10$ Number of electrons in antibonding orbital $=5$ Bond order of $\mathrm{NO}_2^{+}=\frac{10-5}{2}=2.5$ For $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ Molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma 1 s^2 \sigma^* 1 s^2 \sigma 2 s^2 \sigma^* 2 s^2 \pi 2 p_x^2 \pi 2 p_y^2 \sigma 2 p_z^2$ Number of electrons in bonding orbital $=10$ Number of electrons in antibonding orbital $=4$ Bond order $=\frac{10-4}{2}=3$ So, $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}$ and $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ does not have same bond order.

3267.text: If the first ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Be}$ and C respectively are $520,899,1086 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$, the first ionisation enthalpy (in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of B will be
3267.sol:
First ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Be}$ and C respectively are $520,899,1086 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$.
The ionisation energy depend on the
(i) Size of the atom
(ii) effective nuclear charge
(iii) Screening effect
(iv) Penetration effect
(v) Electronic configuration
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Li}-1 \mathrm{ s}^2 2 \mathrm{ s}^1 \\
& \mathrm{Be}-1 \mathrm{ s}^2 2 \mathrm{ s}^2 \\
& \mathrm{ B}-1 \mathrm{ s}^2 2 \mathrm{ s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^1 \\
& \mathrm{C}-1 \mathrm{ s}^2 2 \mathrm{ s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^2
\end{aligned}$
(i) Left to right in the periodic table ionisation enthalpy increase.
(ii) Beryllium have full filled orbital so its ionisation energy is more than boron.
So, order will be.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{C}>\mathrm{Be}>\mathrm{B}>\mathrm{Li} \\
& 1086>899>{----}>520
\end{aligned}$
So, the value of Boron in between 899 to 520 .
$\therefore$ Correct option will be (c). which is 801 value for Boron.

6204.text: The absolute minimum value of $x^4-x^2-2 x+5$ is
6204.sol:
$x^4-x^2-2 x+5=f(x)$ (say)
Then, $f^{\prime}(x)=4 x^3-2 x-2$
Equate $f^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow 4 x^3-2 x-2=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 x^3-x-1=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 x\left(x^2-1\right)+(x-1)=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 x(x-1)(x+1)+(x-1)=0\Rightarrow \quad(x-1)[2 x(x+1)+1]=0\Rightarrow \quad(x-1)\left(2 x^2+2 x+1\right)=0\Rightarrow \quad x-1=0$ and $2 x^2+2 x+1=0\Rightarrow x=1$ and $x=-\frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4-8}}{4}$ (Imaginary)
$\Rightarrow x=1$ and $x=(-1 \pm 1 i) / 2f^{\prime \prime}(x)=12 x^2-2f^{\prime \prime}(x) / x=1=10 > 0\Rightarrow f(x)$ is minimum at $x=1$
Now, $f(\mathrm{l})=(\mathrm{l})^4-(\mathrm{l})^2-2+5=3\therefore$ Absolute minimum value is 3.

6363.text: The radius of a circular plate is increasing at the rate of $0.01 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm{s}$ when the radius is $12 \mathrm{ cm}$. Then, the rate at which the area increases, is
6363.sol:
The area of circular plate is
A=\pi r^2$
On differentiating w.r.t. $t$, we get
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d A}{d t}=2 \pi r \frac{d r}{d t} \\
& \frac{d A}{d t}=2 \pi(12)(0.01) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad {\left[\because \text{ given } \frac{d r}{d t}=0.01 \Rightarrow r=12\right] } \\

6367.text: The sum of two numbers is 20. If the product of the square of one number and cube of the other is maximum, then the numbers are :
6367.sol:
Let the numbers be $x, y$.
$\therefore \quad x+y=20 \Rightarrow y=20-x$
Let $S=x^3(20-x)^2$
On differentiating w.r.t $x$, we get
$\frac{d S}{d x}=2 x^3(20-x)(-1)+3 x^2(20-x)^2$
For maximum or minimum, put $\frac{d S}{d x}=0\Rightarrow \quad x^2(20-x)(-2 x+60-3 x)=0\Rightarrow \quad x=0, x=12$ or $x=20x$ cannot be 0 or 20
When $x=12$, then $y=20-12=8$
The required numbers are 12,8 .

6593.text: The least value of $n$ so that $C3 \left(n - 1\right) + C4 \left(n - 1\right) > C3 n$
6593.sol:
Given:

$C3 \left(n - 1\right) + C4 \left(n - 1\right) > C3 n$

$⇒ C4 - 1 \left(n - 1\right) + C4 \left(n - 1\right) > C3 n$

$⇒ C4 n > C3 n$

$\left[∵ Cr - 1 n + Cr n = Cr n + 1\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{n !}{4 ! \times \left(n - 4\right)$!}$> \dfrac{n !}{3 ! \times \left(n - 3\right) !}$

$⇒ 3 ! \times \left(n - 3\right)$! > 4 ! \times $\left(n - 4\right)$!$

$⇒ 3 ! \times $\left(n - 3\right)\times \left(n - 4\right)$! > 4 \times$3 ! \times \left(n - 4\right)$!$

$⇒ $\left(n - 3\right) >4$

$⇒ n > 7$

So, least value of $n$ is $8$.

It can be noted that if the ball is neither red or green, then it must be blue.

Number of blue balls $= 7$

Now, total number of balls $= 8 + 7 + 6 = 21$

Thus, the probability is $= \dfrac{7}{21} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

& y+1=2(x-2) \\

19656.subject: Chemistry
19656.text:
Which of the following statement/s about nucleic acids is/are correct?
i. The chirality of both DNA and RNA molecules is due to the L-sugar component.
ii. The complementary bases in DNA are adenine \& thymine and guanine \& cytosine.
iii. $\quad \beta$-D-glucopyranose is the sugar moiety present in the RNA molecule.
iv. RNA controls the synthesis of proteins.
19656.sol:
Statement (i) is incorrect because the chirality of DNA and RNA is due to the D-sugar component, specifically D-2-deoxyribose in DNA and D-ribose in RNA.

Statement (ii) is correct. In DNA, adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T) via two hydrogen bonds, and guanine (G) pairs with cytosine (C) via three hydrogen bonds.

Statement (iii) is incorrect. The sugar moiety in RNA is $\beta$-D-ribofuranose, not $\beta$-D-glucopyranose.

Statement (iv) is correct. RNA plays a central role in protein synthesis through the processes of transcription and translation.

Since statements (ii) and (iv) are correct, the correct option is (Vj2Fl).

Answer: (ii) and (iv)

19772.text:
Given below are 4 molecular species/ions. Identify the species/ion which exhibits diamagnetic nature.
$[\mathrm{A}]=\mathrm{N}_2^{+} \quad[\mathrm{B}]=\mathrm{O}_2^{-} \quad[\mathrm{C}]=\mathrm{B}_2 \quad[\mathrm{D}]=\mathrm{C}_2$
19772.sol:
The molecular orbital configuration for each species is determined based on the number of electrons.

For $\mathrm{N_2^{+}}$ (13 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{2}\,\sigma_{2p_z}^{1}$
Since there is one unpaired electron in the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital, it is paramagnetic.

For $\mathrm{O_2^{-}}$ (17 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2p_z}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{*1}$
Since there is one unpaired electron in the $\pi_{2p_y}^{*}$ orbital, it is paramagnetic.

For $\mathrm{B_2}$ (10 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{1}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{1}$
According to Hund's rule, the two electrons in the degenerate $\pi$ orbitals remain unpaired, making it paramagnetic.

For $\mathrm{C_2}$ (12 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{2}$
All electrons are paired; therefore, $\mathrm{C_2}$ is diamagnetic.

Answer: [D]

21399.subject: Mathematics
21399.text: If $f(x)=\dfrac{(x+1)^7 \sqrt{1+x^2}}{\left(x^2-x+1\right)^6}$ then the value of $f^{\prime}(0)$ is equal to
21399.sol:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{(x+1)^7 \sqrt{1+x^2}}{(x^2-x+1)^6}$.

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$\ln f(x) = 7 \ln(x+1) + \dfrac{1}{2} \ln(1+x^2) - 6 \ln(x^2-x+1)$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)} = \dfrac{7}{x+1} + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2x}{1+x^2} - 6 \cdot \dfrac{2x-1}{x^2-x+1}$.

$\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)} = \dfrac{7}{x+1} + \dfrac{x}{1+x^2} - \dfrac{6(2x-1)}{x^2-x+1}$.

Evaluating at $x=0$:

$f(0) = \dfrac{(0+1)^7 \sqrt{1+0^2}}{(0^2-0+1)^6} = \dfrac{1 \times 1}{1} = 1$.

Substituting $x=0$ into the derivative expression:

$\dfrac{f'(0)}{f(0)} = \dfrac{7}{0+1} + \dfrac{0}{1+0^2} - \dfrac{6(2(0)-1)}{0^2-0+1}$.

$\dfrac{f'(0)}{1} = 7 + 0 - 6(-1) = 7 + 6 = 13$.

Therefore, $f'(0) = 13$.

Answer: 13

22357.subject: Physics
22357.text: A solenoid having resistance $R = 60\ \Omega$ and inductance $L = 0.4\ H$ is connected to an AC source $V = 100\sqrt{2}\sin 200t$. Find the maximum current.
22357.sol:
Given the AC source equation $V = 100\sqrt{2}\sin(200t)$, the peak voltage is $V_m = 100\sqrt{2}\ \text{V}$ and the angular frequency is $\omega = 200\ \text{rad/s}$.

The inductive reactance of the solenoid is:
$X_L = \omega L = 200 \times 0.4 = 80\ \Omega$

The impedance of the circuit is:
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{60^2 + 80^2} = \sqrt{3600 + 6400} = 100\ \Omega$

The maximum (peak) current in the circuit is:
$I_m = \dfrac{V_m}{Z} = \dfrac{100\sqrt{2}}{100} = \sqrt{2}\ \text{A}$

Since $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$, the maximum current is $1.414\ \text{A}$.

Answer: $1.414\ \text{A}$

23366.subject: Physics
23366.text: To a fish under water, viewing obliquely, a fisherman standing on the bank of a lake looks
options: Taller than what he actually is
Same height as he actually is
Taller or shorter depending on the refractive index of water
Shorter than what he actually is
23366.sol:
When a fish looks at an object outside the water, the light rays travel from the rarer medium (air) to the denser medium (water).

According to the laws of refraction, when light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it bends towards the normal.

Let the height of the fisherman be $h$. The light rays coming from the top of the fisherman's head and his feet enter the water and bend towards the normal at the water surface.

Due to this refraction, the apparent position of the fisherman appears to be shifted upwards. Specifically, the rays appear to originate from a point further away from the surface than the actual object.

The apparent height $h'$ is given by $h' = \mu h$, where $\mu$ is the refractive index of water relative to air (\mu \approx 1.33$).

Since \mu > 1$, the apparent height $h'$ is greater than the actual height $h$.

Therefore, the fisherman appears taller than he actually is.

Answer: Taller than what he actually is

23710.subject: Physics
23710.text: An open pipe is in second harmonic with frequency $f_1$. One end of the tube is closed and frequency is increased to $f_2$ and it resonates again with nth harmonic. For what value of n , the ratio of $\dfrac{f_1}{f_2}$ is $\dfrac{4}{5}$ ?
23710.sol:
For an open pipe of length $L$, the frequency of the second harmonic is given by $f_1 = 2 \times \dfrac{v}{2L} = \dfrac{v}{L}$, where $v$ is the speed of sound.

When one end is closed, the pipe becomes a closed pipe of length $L$. The frequencies of a closed pipe are given by $f = m \dfrac{v}{4L}$, where $m$ is an odd integer ($1, 3, 5, \dots$). The $n$-th harmonic of a closed pipe corresponds to the $n$-th odd harmonic, so $f_2 = n \dfrac{v}{4L}$, where $n$ is an odd integer.

The ratio of the frequencies is given as $\dfrac{f_1}{f_2} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Substituting the expressions for $f_1$ and $f_2$:

$\dfrac{v/L}{n v / 4L} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$\dfrac{4}{n} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Therefore, $n = 5$.

Answer: 5

24471.subject: Chemistry
24471.text:
Match the major products obtained in the reactions given in List-I with the corresponding structures in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) (1)
(Q) (2)
(R) (3)
(S) (4)
(5)
24471.sol:
For the reaction in (P), 2-bromo-5-nitrobenzaldehyde oxime reacts with aqueous NaOH. The strong base deprotonates the oxime group. The resulting oximate anion undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($S_NAr$), attacking the ortho-carbon and displacing the bromide ion to form a 1,2-benzisoxazole intermediate. Since it is derived from an aldoxime, this intermediate has a hydrogen atom at the C3 position. In the presence of NaOH, it undergoes base-catalyzed Kemp elimination (ring opening) to form 2-hydroxy-5-nitrobenzonitrile, which corresponds to structure (1). Thus, P $\rightarrow$ 1.

In reaction (Q), the aldoxime is treated with acetic anhydride, which acetylates the oxime group to form an O-acetate. Subsequent treatment with the mild base $Na_2CO_3$ causes the elimination of acetic acid, converting the aldoxime acetate into a nitrile. The bromide is not displaced under these mild conditions. The product is 2-bromo-5-nitrobenzonitrile, which corresponds to structure (2). Thus, Q $\rightarrow$ 2.

For the reaction in (R), 2-bromo-5-nitroacetophenone oxime reacts with aqueous NaOH. Similar to (P), the oximate anion is formed and displaces the ortho-bromide via $S_NAr$ to form a 1,2-benzisoxazole ring. However, because it is derived from a ketoxime, there is a methyl group at the C3 position instead of a hydrogen. Therefore, Kemp elimination cannot occur, and the reaction stops at the stable 3-methyl-5-nitro-1,2-benzisoxazole, which corresponds to structure (4). Thus, R $\rightarrow$ 4.

In reaction (S), the O-acetate of the ketoxime is treated with aqueous $Na_2CO_3$. Since it is a ketoxime derivative, it cannot undergo elimination to form a nitrile. The mild base simply hydrolyzes the acetate group back to the oxime. The base is not strong enough to promote the subsequent $S_NAr$ ring closure. The product is 2-bromo-5-nitroacetophenone oxime, which corresponds to structure (5). Thus, S $\rightarrow$ 5.

Combining these results gives the sequence P $\rightarrow$ 1, Q $\rightarrow$ 2, R $\rightarrow$ 4, S $\rightarrow$ 5.

Answer: P $\rightarrow$ 1; Q $\longrightarrow$ 2; R $\rightarrow$ 4; S $\longrightarrow$ 5

25568.text:
Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of

$\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11)) + 10 \sin\left(2 \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right) + 10 \sin(2 \tan^{-1}(2))$

is
25568.sol:
For the first term, $\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11))$:
The principal value branch of $\cot^{-1}(x)$ is $(0, \pi)$.
Since the cotangent function is periodic with period $\pi$, $\cot(-11) = \cot(-11 + 4\pi)$.
Using $\pi \approx 3.14$, we have $4\pi \approx 12.56$, so $-11 + 4\pi \approx 1.56$, which lies in the interval $(0, \pi)$.
Thus, $\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11)) = 4\pi - 11$.

For the second term, $10 \sin\left(2 \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right)$:
Since $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, we get:
$10 \sin\left(2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 10 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 10(1) = 10$.

For the third term, $10 \sin(2 \tan^{-1}(2))$:
Let $\theta = \tan^{-1}(2) \Rightarrow \tan(\theta) = 2$.
Using the multiple angle formula $\sin(2\theta) = \dfrac{2\tan(\theta)}{1 + \tan^2(\theta)}$, we obtain:
$\sin(2\theta) = \dfrac{2(2)}{1 + 2^2} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.
Therefore, $10 \sin(2 \tan^{-1}(2)) = 10 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 8$.

Adding the three evaluated terms together:
$(4\pi - 11) + 10 + 8 = 4\pi + 7$.

Answer: $4\pi + 7$

27379.subject: Chemistry
27379.text: The test to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines is:
27379.sol:
The Hinsberg test, which can distinguish primary, secondary, and tertiary amines, is based upon sulfonamide formation. In the Hinsberg test, an amine is reacted with benzene sulfonyl chloride. If a product forms, the amine is either a primary or secondary amine, because tertiary amines do not form stable sulfonamides. If the sulfonamide that forms dissolves in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution, it is a primary amine. If the sulfonamide is insoluble in aqueous sodium hydroxide, it is a secondary amine

Benzene sulphonyl chloride is Hinsberg reagent.

28497.text: The successive 5 ionisation energies of an element are $800,2427,3658,25024$ and $32824 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$, respectively. By using the above values predict the group in which the above element is present :
28497.sol:
The successive 5 ionisation energies of an element are 800,2427,3658,25024 and $32824 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$, respectively.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{IE}_2}{\mathrm{IE}_1}=\frac{2427}{800}=3.03 \\
& \frac{\mathrm{IE}}{\mathrm{IE}_2}=\frac{3658}{2427}=1.51 \\
& \frac{\mathrm{IE}}{\mathrm{IE}_3}=\frac{25024}{3658}=6.84
\end{aligned} \frac{\mathrm{IE}_5}{\mathrm{IE}_4}=\frac{32824}{25024}=1.31$
Since ( $\mathrm{IE}_4 / \mathrm{IE}_3$ ) value is maximum, the element belongs to group 13.

32861.text: A water tank has the shape of a right circular cone with axis vertical and vertex downwards. Its semivertical angle is $\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{3}{4}$. Plotting the diagram we have,

Now given, $tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{r}{h}$ and let water is poured at constant rate $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 6$ cubic meter per hour,

Now we know that volume of cone is given by $V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi{r}^{2}h = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi{h}^{3}\tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{9\pi}{48}{h}^{3} = \dfrac{3\pi}{16}{h}^{3}$ $\left\{\text{by using}tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{r}{h}\right\}$

Now differentiating above equation we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{3\pi}{16} \cdot 3{h}^{2} \cdot \dfrac{dh}{dt} = 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3\pi}\text{m/hr}$

Now, we know that curved surface area of cone is given by,

$S = \pirl = \dfrac{15}{16}\pi{h}^{2}$ $\left\{\text{as}sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{r}{l} ⇒ l = \dfrac{5}{3}r\text{and}r = \dfrac{3}{4}h\right\}$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dS}{dt} = \dfrac{15\pi}{16} \cdot 2h\dfrac{dh}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dS}{dt} = 5{m}^{2} / hr$ $\left\{\text{as}\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3\pi}\text{m/hr}\right\}$

33645.text: Let the circle $S: 36{x}^{2} + 36{y}^{2} - 108x + 120y + C = 0$ be such that it neither intersects nor touches the co-ordinate axes. If the point of intersection of the lines, $x - 2y = 4$ and $2x - y = 5$ lies inside the circle $S,$ then:
33645.sol:
The given circle is $S: 36{x}^{2} + 36{y}^{2} - 108x + 120y + C = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 3x + \dfrac{10}{3}y + \dfrac{C}{36} = 0$

We know that the centre and radius of a circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ is $\left(- g, - f\right)$ and $\sqrt{{g}^{2} + {f}^{2} - c}$ respectively.

Thus, centre $e ≡ \left(- g, - f\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, - \dfrac{10}{6}\right)$ and radius $= r = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{100}{36} - \dfrac{C}{36}}$

Now, this circle neither intersects nor touches the co-ordinate axes, hence, the radius of the circle is less than the absolute value of the co-ordinate with smaller value.

$⇒ r < \dfrac{3}{2}$

$\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{100}{36} - \dfrac{C}{36}} < \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{100}{36} - \dfrac{C}{36} < \dfrac{9}{4}$

$⇒ C > 100 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now, point of intersection of $x - 2y = 4$ and $2x - y = 5$ is $( 2, - 1 ) ,$ which lies inside the circle $S .$

The point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ lies inside a circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0,$ if ${x}_{1}^{2} + {y}_{1}^{2} + 2g{x}_{1} + 2f{y}_{1} + c < 0$

$⇒ {\left(2\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 1\right)}^{2} - 3\left(2\right) + \dfrac{10}{3}\left(- 1\right) + \dfrac{C}{36} < 0$

$⇒ 4 + 1 - 6 - \dfrac{10}{3} + \dfrac{C}{36} < 0$

$⇒ C < 156 \ldots \left(2\right)$

From $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right),$ we have $100 < C < 156$

33913.text:
Let ${z}_{1} and {z}_{2}$ be any two non-zero complex numbers such that $3\left|{z}_{1}\right| = 4\left|{z}_{2}\right| .$ If $z = \dfrac{3{z}_{1}}{2{z}_{2}} + \dfrac{2{z}_{2}}{3{z}_{1}}$ then maximum value of $\left|z\right|$ is

Note: In actual paper value of $\left|z\right|$ was asked. Hence, none of the options given were correct. So we have modified the question as well as options.
33913.sol:
Let $arg\left(\dfrac{3{z}_{1}}{2{z}_{2}}\right) = \theta,$ and we know that, if the $arg\left(z\right) = \alpha,$ then $arg\left(\dfrac{1}{z}\right) = - \alpha .$

$∴ arg\left(\dfrac{2{z}_{2}}{3{z}_{1}}\right) = - \theta$

Also, we know that a complex number $w$ can be expressed as $w = \left|w\right|\left(cos\alpha + isin\alpha\right),$ where $\alpha$ is the argument of the complex number.

$∴ z = \dfrac{3}{2}\left|\dfrac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}}\right|\left(cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{2}{3}\left|\dfrac{{z}_{2}}{{z}_{1}}\right|\left(cos\theta - isin\theta\right)$

Given, $3\left|{z}_{1}\right| = 4\left|{z}_{2}\right|, ⇒ \left|\dfrac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}}\right| = \dfrac{4}{3},$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{3}\left(cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{4}\left(cos\theta - isin\theta\right)$

$⇒ z = 2\left(cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(cos\theta - isin\theta\right)$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{5}{2}cos\theta + \left(\dfrac{3}{2}sin\theta\right)i$

$∴ \left|z\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}\cos^{2}\theta + \dfrac{9}{4}\sin^{2}\theta}$

Now, using $\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1,$ we get

$\left|z\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}\cos^{2}\theta + \dfrac{9}{4}\left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right)}$

$⇒ \left|z\right| = \sqrt{4\cos^{2}\theta + \dfrac{9}{4}}$

And, we know that the maximum value of $cos\theta$ is $1 .$
$∴ {\left|z\right|}_{max} = \sqrt{4 + \dfrac{9}{4}} = \dfrac{5}{2} .$

Similarly $f\left(2 + 1\right) = f\left(2\right) \cdot f\left(1\right) ⇒ f\left(3\right) = {3}^{2} \times 3 = {3}^{3}$

So, $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}f\left(r\right) = 3279$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) + f\left(2\right) + f\left(3\right) . . . . . . . f\left(n\right) = 3279$

$⇒ 3 + {3}^{2} + {3}^{3} . . . . . . . + {3}^{n} = 3279$

$⇒ \dfrac{{3}^{n} - 1}{2} = 1093$

$⇒ {3}^{n} - 1 = 2186$

$⇒ {3}^{n} = 2187$

$⇒ {3}^{n} = {3}^{7}$

$⇒ n = 7$

37018.text: Let $A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots, A_{39}$ be $39$ arithmetic means between the numbers $59$ and $159$. Then the mean of $A_{25}, A_{28}, A_{31}$ and $A_{36}$ is equal to :
37018.sol:
The sequence $59, A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_{39}, 159$ forms an arithmetic progression with $41$ terms.

The common difference $d$ is given by $d = \dfrac{159 - 59}{39 + 1} = \dfrac{100}{40} = 2.5$

The $k$-th arithmetic mean is $A_k = 59 + k \cdot d$

The required mean is $\dfrac{A_{25} + A_{28} + A_{31} + A_{36}}{4}$

$\dfrac{A_{25} + A_{28} + A_{31} + A_{36}}{4} = \dfrac{(59 + 25d) + (59 + 28d) + (59 + 31d) + (59 + 36d)}{4}$

$= \dfrac{4 \times 59 + 120d}{4} = 59 + 30d$

Substituting $d = 2.5$:

$= 59 + 30(2.5) = 59 + 75 = 134$

Answer: $134$

$\dfrac{{1}^{3} + {2}^{3} + {3}^{3} . . . . . . . {n}^{3}}{1 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 5 + 3 \cdot 7 + . . . . n\left(2n + 1\right)} = \dfrac{9}{5}$

Now we know that ${1}^{3} + {2}^{3} + {3}^{3} . . . . . . . {n}^{3} = {\left[\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}\right]}^{2}$

And $Σn\left(2n + 1\right) = 2Σ{n}^{2} + Σn$

$⇒ Σn\left(2n + 1\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{6} + \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}$

$⇒ Σn\left(2n + 1\right) = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{3} + \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}$

So putting the value in the given equation we get,

$\dfrac{{1}^{3} + {2}^{3} + {3}^{3} . . . . . . . {n}^{3}}{1 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 5 + 3 \cdot 7 + . . . . n\left(2n + 1\right)} = \dfrac{9}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left[\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}\right]}^{2}}{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{3} + \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}} = \dfrac{9}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4}\left[n\left(n + 1\right)\right]}{\dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{9}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{6\left[n\left(n + 1\right)\right]}{4\left(2\left(2n + 1\right) + 3\right)} = \dfrac{9}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left[n\left(n + 1\right)\right]}{2\left(2\left(2n + 1\right) + 3\right)} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$⇒ 5\left[n\left(n + 1\right)\right] = 6\left(2\left(2n + 1\right) + 3\right)$

$⇒ 5{n}^{2} + 5n = 6\left(4n + 5\right)$

$⇒ 5{n}^{2} + 5n = 24n + 30$

$⇒ 5{n}^{2} - 19n - 30 = 0$

$⇒ 5{n}^{2} - 25n + 6n - 30 = 0$

$⇒ \left(5n + 6\right)\left(n - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ n = 5$

38344.text: If $0 < x, y < \pi$ and $cosx + cosy - cos\left(x + y\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$, then $sinx + cosy$ is equal to:
38344.sol:
$cosx + cosy - cos\left(x + y\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$2cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) - \left[2\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) - 1\right] = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$2cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) - 2\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) + 1 = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$2cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) - 2\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$4cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) - 4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = 1$

$⇒ 4cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) - 4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = 1 = \sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) + \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)$

$⇒ 4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) + \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) - 4cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) + \sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ {\left(2cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) - cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)\right)}^{2} + \sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ sin\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) = 0$ and $cos\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}cos\left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)$

⇒ x = y and $cosx = \dfrac{1}{2} = cosy$

$∴ sinx = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ sinx + cosy = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{2}$

option $\left(4\right)$

since $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$, so $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} \cdot \overset{\to}{\alpha} = 0$

$⇒ $\left[\left(1 - 4t\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left(2 - 3t\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(- 4 - 5t\right)$\overset{^}{k}\right] \cdot $\left[4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right]$ = 0$

$⇒ 4$\left(1 - 4t\right)$ + 3$\left(2 - 3t\right)$ + 5$\left(- 4 - 5t\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ 4 - 16t + 6 - 9t - 20 - 25t = 0$

$⇒ - 50t = 10⇒ t = $\dfrac{- 1}{5}

From \left(2\right)$ and $\left(3\right), we get$\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = $\dfrac{- 1}{5}\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \dfrac{9}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{13}{5}\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k} = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(9\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} - 15\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, the $value of5\overset{\to}{\beta}2 \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) will be,$

$= 5 \times \dfrac{1}{5} ($ 9\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} - 15\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot $\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ = 9 + 13 - 15 = 7$

38655.subject: Mathematics
38655.text: The sum of the distinct real values of $\mu$ for which the vectors $\mu\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \mu\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \mu\overset{^}{k}$ are co-planar, is
38655.sol:
Given the three vectors are coplanar.

Hence, $\left|\begin{cases}\mu & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \mu & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \mu\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \mu\left({\mu}^{2} - 1\right) - 1\left(\mu - 1\right) + 1\left(1 - \mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ \mu\left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu + 1\right) - 2\left(\mu - 1\right) = 0\left[∵ {a}^{2} - {b}^{2} = \left(a - b\right)\left(a + b\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu\left(\mu + 1\right) - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left({\mu}^{2} + \mu + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \mu = 1, 1, - 2$

Therefore, the sum of the distinct real values of $\mu = - 2 + 1 = - 1$.

38826.text: An AC source is connected to an inductance of $100mH$, a capacitance of $100\muF$ and a resistance of $120Ω$ as shown in figure. The time in which the resistance having a thermal capacity $2J C - 1 ∘$ will get heated by $16 ° C$ is _____ $s$.
38826.sol:
From the diagram given,

Angular frequency $\omega = 100rad{s}^{- 1}$ and ${V}_{rms} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{20\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 20V$.

Now, ${X}_{L} = \omegaL = 100 \times 100 \times {10}^{- 3} = 10Ω$ and ${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 100 \times {10}^{- 6}} = 100Ω$

$\left|\left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)\right| = \left|10 - 100\right| = 90Ω$

The impedance of the circuit,

$Z = \sqrt{{\left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)}^{2} + {R}^{2}} = \sqrt{{\left(90\right)}^{2} + {\left(120\right)}^{2}} = 150Ω$

The current in the circuit,

${i}_{mrs} = \dfrac{{V}_{rms}}{Z} = \left(\dfrac{20}{150}\right)A$

Power factor $cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

Now

$\left({V}_{rms}{i}_{rms}cosϕ\right)\Deltat = ms\left(\DeltaT\right) ⇒ \Deltat = \dfrac{ms\left(\DeltaT\right)}{{V}_{rms} \times \dfrac{{V}_{rms}}{Z} \times \dfrac{R}{Z}} = \dfrac{ms\left(\DeltaT\right){Z}^{2}}{{{V}_{rms}}^{2} \times R} = \dfrac{2 \times 16 \times 22500}{400 \times 120} = 15s$

$⇒ \Deltat = 15s$

40392.sol:
The speed of electromagnetic wave in free space is given by

$\mathrm{C}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_{0} \epsilon_{0}}}$

In medium, $\mathbf{v}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{k} \in_{0} \mu_{0}}} \ldots$ (ii)

Dividing equation (i) by(ii), we get $\therefore \frac{\mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{V}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{k}}=\mathrm{n}$

$\frac{1}{2} \epsilon_{0} \mathrm{E}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{C}=$ intensity $=\frac{1}{2} \epsilon_{0} \mathrm{kE}^{2} \mathrm{v}$

$\therefore \mathrm{E}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{kE}^{2} \mathrm{v}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{E_{0}^{2}}{E^{2}}=\frac{k V}{C}=\frac{n^{2}}{n} \Rightarrow \frac{E_{0}}{E}=\sqrt{n}$

similarly

$\frac{\mathrm{B}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{C}}{2 \mu_{0}}=\frac{\mathrm{B}^{2} \mathrm{v}}{2 \mu_{0}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{B}_{0}}{\mathrm{~B}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{n}}}$

47265.text: The Annual Net Primary Productivity on land and ocean respectively are ____ and ____ billion tons.
47265.sol:
The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately $170$ billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter.

Out of this total, the productivity of the oceans is only $55$ billion tons, despite occupying about $70$ percent of the Earth's surface.

The productivity on land is the remaining amount, which is $170 - 55 = 115$ billion tons.

Therefore, the annual net primary productivity on land and ocean respectively are $115$ and $55$ billion tons.

Answer: $115, 55$

47966.subject: Chemistry
47966.text: The compound from which chlorobenzene cannot be prepared easily is
47966.sol:
Chlorobenzene can be easily prepared from aniline by first converting it to benzene diazonium chloride, followed by the Sandmeyer reaction.

Chlorobenzene can be easily prepared from benzene by electrophilic aromatic substitution using $Cl_2$ in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst like $FeCl_3$ or $AlCl_3$.

Chlorobenzene can be easily prepared from benzene diazonium chloride by treating it with $Cu_2Cl_2$ and $HCl$ (Sandmeyer reaction).

In phenol, the carbon-oxygen bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance between the lone pairs on oxygen and the benzene ring. This makes the $C-O$ bond stronger and difficult to cleave. Therefore, nucleophilic substitution of the hydroxyl group by a chloride ion (using reagents like $PCl_5$ or $SOCl_2$) is very difficult, and chlorobenzene cannot be prepared easily from phenol.

Answer: Phenol

The given integral is $I = \int \dfrac{\sin^n x}{\cos^{n+2} x} \,dx$

Substituting these into the integral, we get:

$I = \int t^n \,dt$

$I = \dfrac{t^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$

$I = \dfrac{\tan^{n+1} x}{n+1} + C$

Answer: $\dfrac{\tan^{n+1} x}{n + 1} + C$

50441.subject: Physics
50441.text: Two bodies are projected with the same velocity. If one is projected at an angle of $30^{}^{\circ}$ and the other at $45^{}^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, then the ratio of maximum heights attained is
50441.sol:
The maximum height attained by a projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$.

For the first body, $\theta_1 = 30^{}^{\circ}$:
$H_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 30^{}^{\circ}}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2}{2g} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{u^2}{8g}$

For the second body, $\theta_2 = 45^{}^{\circ}$:
$H_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 45^{}^{\circ}}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2}{2g} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{u^2}{4g}$

The ratio of maximum heights is:
$\dfrac{H_1}{H_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{u^2}{8g}}{\dfrac{u^2}{4g}} = \dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, the ratio is $1:2$.

Answer: $1:2$

56661.subject: Chemistry
56661.text: Identify the lanthanoid that exhibits zero effective magnetic moment in +3 state.
56661.sol:
A species exhibits zero effective magnetic moment only if it contains no unpaired electrons. For lanthanoid ions in the +3 oxidation state, we analyze their electronic configurations to determine which one has no unpaired electrons.

Holmium (Ho, atomic number 67):
Ground state configuration is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{11} 6s^2$, so $\mathrm{Ho}^{3+}$ has $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{10}$.
With 10 electrons in 7 orbitals, there are 4 unpaired electrons according to Hund’s rule.

Praseodymium (Pr, atomic number 59):
Ground state is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{3} 6s^2$, so $\mathrm{Pr}^{3+}$ is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{2}$.
This yields 2 unpaired electrons.

Erbium (Er, atomic number 68):
Ground state is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{12} 6s^2$, so $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{11}$.
This gives 3 unpaired electrons.

Lutetium (Lu, atomic number 71):
Ground state is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{1} 6s^2$, so $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ has $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{14}$.
This is a completely filled $f$ subshell with all electrons paired, resulting in zero unpaired electrons.

Therefore, only $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ exhibits zero effective magnetic moment.

58001.text: Calculate the ionic concentration of sparingly soluble salt BA in mol dm ${ }^{-3}$ at 300 K when equilibrium is attained if solubility product of salt is $2.7 \times 10^{-10}$ at same temperature.

$\text{BA(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{B}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{A}^-\text{(aq)}$

Let $s$ represent the molar solubility in mol dm^{-3}$. At equilibrium, concentrations are $[$\text{B}^+] =$ s$ and $[$\text{A}^-] =$ s$.

The solubility product is $K_{sp} = [$\text{B}^+][\text{A}^-] =$ s^2$.

Given $K_{sp} = 2.7 \times 10^{-10}$, solving for $s$ gives:

$s^2 = 2.7 \times 10^{-10}$
$s = $\sqrt{2.7 \times 10^{-10}} \approx$1.64 \times 10^{-5}$ mol dm^{-3}$

This value corresponds to option D.

61259.subject: Mathematics
61259.text: $The general solution of the differential equation \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = x^2 + 5$ is....
61259.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{x}y = x^2 + 5$.

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$, where $P = \dfrac{1}{x}$ and $Q = x^2 + 5$.

The integrating factor is $e^{\int P dx} = e^{\int \dfrac{1}{x} dx} = e^{\ln x} = x$.

Multiplying the equation by the integrating factor, the solution is given by:

$y \cdot x = \int x(x^2 + 5) dx + C$

$xy = \int (x^3 + 5x) dx + C$

$xy = \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} + C$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - xy = -C$

Taking $-C = c$, the general solution is:

$\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - xy = c$

Answer: $\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - xy = c$

63315.subject: Mathematics
63315.text: If two lines represented by $x^2 - (1 + \sqrt{3})xy + \sqrt{3}y^2 = 0$ make angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the X-axis, then $\tan(\alpha + \beta)$ is...
63315.sol:
The given equation of the pair of straight lines is $x^2 - (1 + \sqrt{3})xy + \sqrt{3}y^2 = 0$.

Dividing the entire equation by $x^2$, we get:

$\sqrt{3}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2 - (1 + \sqrt{3})\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + 1 = 0$

Let $m = \dfrac{y}{x}$. The slopes of the two lines, $m_1 = \tan \alpha$ and $m_2 = \tan \beta$, are the roots of the quadratic equation:

$\sqrt{3}m^2 - (1 + \sqrt{3})m + 1 = 0$

From the properties of quadratic equations, the sum and product of the roots are:

$\tan \alpha + \tan \beta = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\tan \alpha \tan \beta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Using the trigonometric identity for the tangent of a sum:

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\tan \alpha + \tan \beta}{1 - \tan \alpha \tan \beta}$

Substituting the values, we get:

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}$

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}}{\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3}}}$

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$

63326.subject: Mathematics
63326.text: The triangle formed by the lines $2x^2 - 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$ and $3x - y = 7$ is...
63326.sol:
The given equation of the pair of straight lines is $2x^2 - 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$.

Factorizing the equation:

$2x^2 - 4xy + xy - 2y^2 = 0$

$2x(x - 2y) + y(x - 2y) = 0$

$(2x + y)(x - 2y) = 0$

The equations of the two lines are $L_1: 2x + y = 0$ and $L_2: x - 2y = 0$.

The slopes of these lines are $m_1 = -2$ and $m_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $m_1 m_2 = -2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = -1$, the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ are perpendicular to each other. Thus, the triangle is right-angled.

The equation of the third line is $L_3: 3x - y = 7$, which has a slope $m_3 = 3$.

Let $\theta_1$ be the angle between $L_1$ and $L_3$:

$\tan \theta_1 = \left| \dfrac{m_1 - m_3}{1 + m_1 m_3} \right| = \left| \dfrac{-2 - 3}{1 + (-2)(3)} \right| = \left| \dfrac{-5}{-5} \right| = 1$

$\Rightarrow \theta_1 = 45^{}^{\circ}$

Let $\theta_2$ be the angle between $L_2$ and $L_3$:

$\tan \theta_2 = \left| \dfrac{m_2 - m_3}{1 + m_2 m_3} \right| = \left| \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - 3}{1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(3)} \right| = \left| \dfrac{-\dfrac{5}{2}}{\dfrac{5}{2}} \right| = 1$

$\Rightarrow \theta_2 = 45^{}^{\circ}$

Since two angles of the right-angled triangle are $45^{}^{\circ}$, the triangle is right-angled isosceles.

Answer: Right angled isosceles

63452.subject: Mathematics
63452.text: The equation of the directrix of the parabola $y^2+4 y+4 x+2=0$ is
63452.sol:
Finding the directrix of the parabola defined by y²+4y+4x+2=0.

Rewriting the equation by completing the square for the y-terms: $y^2+4y+4 = -4x-2+4$, resulting in $(y+2)^2 = -4x+2$.

Factoring the right side yields $(y+2)^2 = -4(x - 1/2)$.

This matches the standard form $(y-k)^2 = -4a(x-h)$, with vertex at $(1/2, -2)$ and $a=1$.

The directrix for this left-opening parabola is $x = h+a = 1/2 + 1 = 3/2$.

Final answer: $x = 3/2$

63586.subject: Mathematics
63586.text:
The Variance of the following probability distribution of X is
X$0$$1$$2$$3$
P(X)$q^3$$3q^2 p$$3qp^2$$p^3$
where $0 < p < 1, q = 1 - p$
63586.sol:
The given probability distribution represents a binomial distribution with parameters $n = 3$ and probability of success $p$, since $P(X = x) = ^{3}C_{x} p^x q^{3-x}$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$.

For a binomial distribution, the variance is given by $npq$.

Substituting $n = 3$, the variance is $3pq$.

Alternatively, calculating the variance using expectations:

$E(X) = \sum x P(x) = 0(q^3) + 1(3q^2 p) + 2(3qp^2) + 3(p^3)$

$E(X) = 3p(q^2 + 2pq + p^2) = 3p(q+p)^2 = 3p$

$E(X^2) = \sum x^2 P(x) = 0(q^3) + 1(3q^2 p) + 4(3qp^2) + 9(p^3)$

$E(X^2) = 3p(q^2 + 4pq + 3p^2) = 3p((q+p)^2 + 2p(q+p)) = 3p(1 + 2p) = 3p + 6p^2$

$\text{Variance} = E(X^2) - (E(X))^2$

$\text{Variance} = 3p + 6p^2 - (3p)^2 = 3p - 3p^2 = 3p(1-p) = 3pq$

Answer: $3pq$

63761.subject: Mathematics
63761.text: Three critics review a book. For the three critics the odds in favor of the book are $2: 5$, $3: 4$ and $4: 3$ respectively. The probability that the majority is in favor of the book, is given by
63761.sol:
The probability that the first critic favors the book is $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=\frac{2}{2+5}=\frac{2}{7}\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{A}^{\prime}\right)=1-\frac{2}{7}=\frac{5}{7}$
The probability that the second critic favors the book is $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=\frac{3}{3+4}=\frac{3}{7}\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{B}^{\prime}\right)=1-\frac{3}{7}=\frac{4}{7}$
The probability that the third critic favors the book is $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})=\frac{4}{4+3}=\frac{4}{7}\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{C}^{\prime}\right)=1-\frac{4}{7}=\frac{3}{7}\therefore \quad$ Majority will be in favor of the book if at least two critics favor the book.
Hence, the probability is
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B} \cap \mathrm{C}^{\prime}\right)+\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B}^{\prime} \cap \mathrm{C}\right) \\
& \quad+\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{A}^{\prime} \cap \mathrm{B} \cap \mathrm{C}\right)+\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B} \cap \mathrm{C}) \\
& =\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B}) \cdot \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{C}^{\prime}\right)+\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}) \cdot \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{B}^{\prime}\right) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C}) \\
& \quad+\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{A}^{\prime}\right) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B}) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})+\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B}) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C}) \\

65885.subject: Physics
65885.text:
Using Bohr's quantisation condition, what is the rotational energy in the second orbit for a diatomic molecule?
(I=$ moment of inertia of diatomic molecule and $h=$ Planck's constant)$
65885.sol:
Rotational energy quantization for a diatomic molecule

The angular momentum $L$ is quantized by Bohr's condition: $L = J\frac{h}{2\pi}$, where $J$ is the rotational quantum number.

For the second orbit, $J = 2$, yielding $L = 2\frac{h}{2\pi} = \frac{h}{\pi}$.

Rotational energy $E_R$ relates to angular momentum through $E_R = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$ with $L = I\omega$, giving $\omega = \frac{L}{I}$.

Substitution results in $E_R = \frac{1}{2}I\left(\frac{L}{I}\right)^2 = \frac{L^2}{2I}$.

Inserting the quantized $L$ value, $E_R = \frac{\left(\frac{h}{\pi}\right)^2}{2I} = \frac{h^2}{2I\pi^2}$.

This matches option B: $\frac{h^2}{2I\pi^2}$.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

67012.subject: Physics
67012.text: A point charge 'Q' is placed at the centre of the line joining two equal charges '+q' and '+q'. The value of 'Q' when the system is in equilibrium is
67012.sol:
Let the two equal charges $+q$ be placed at a distance $r$ from each other.

The charge $Q$ is placed at the centre, so its distance from each $+q$ charge is $\dfrac{r}{2}$.

For the system to be in equilibrium, the net force on each charge must be zero.

The net force on the central charge $Q$ is zero for any value of $Q$ due to symmetry.

For the charge $+q$ to be in equilibrium, the force exerted by the other $+q$ charge must be equal and opposite to the force exerted by $Q$.

The force on $+q$ due to the other $+q$ is $F_1 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q^2}{r^2}$.

The force on $+q$ due to $Q$ is $F_2 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{qQ}{(\dfrac{r}{2})^2} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{4qQ}{r^2}$.

Equating the sum of forces to zero:

$F_1 + F_2 = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q^2}{r^2} + \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{4qQ}{r^2} = 0$

$q^2 + 4qQ = 0$

$Q = \dfrac{-q}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-q}{4}$

67223.subject: Physics
67223.text: A body weighs 45 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force on a body due to earth at a height equal to half the radius of earth will be
67223.sol:
The weight $W = 45\,\text{N}$ on Earth's surface satisfies $W = \frac{GMm}{R^2}$.

At height $h = R/2$, the gravitational force becomes $F' = \frac{GMm}{(R + h)^2} = \frac{GMm}{(3R/2)^2} = \frac{4}{9} \cdot \frac{GMm}{R^2}$.

Substituting the expression for weight yields $F' = \frac{4}{9}W = \frac{4}{9} \cdot 45 = 20\,\text{N}$.

The gravitational force at half Earth's radius is $20\,\text{N}$.

From the given figure, the cross-sectional area of the tube at end P is less than the cross-sectional area at end Q, so $A_P < A_Q$.

According to the equation of continuity for an incompressible fluid, the product of cross-sectional area and velocity remains constant:

$A_P v_P = A_Q v_Q$

Since $A_P < A_Q$, the velocity of the fluid at P is greater than the velocity at Q, which gives $v_P > v_Q$.

The kinetic energy per unit volume of the fluid is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v^2$, where $\rho$ is the density of the fluid.

Since $v_P > v_Q$, it follows that $v_P^2 > v_Q^2$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_P^2 > \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_Q^2$, which implies $K_P > K_Q$.

Answer: $K_P > K_Q$

68704.text: An object of mass 0.2 kg executes simple harmonic oscillations along the $X$ - axis with frequency of $\left(\frac{25}{\pi}\right) \mathrm{Hz}$. At the position $x=0.04 \mathrm{~m}$, the object has kinetic energy 1 J and potential energy 0.6 J . The amplitude of oscillation is
68704.sol:
The total energy for simple harmonic motion is conserved and equals the sum of kinetic and potential energy at any point. Given
$KE = 1\ \text{J}$ and $PE = 0.6\ \text{J}$,

$E = KE + PE = 1 + 0.6 = 1.6\ \text{J}$.

The angular frequency is derived from the frequency
$f = \frac{25}{\pi}\ \text{Hz}$ as
$\omega = 2 \pi f = 2\pi \cdot \frac{25}{\pi} = 50\ \text{rad/s}$.

The spring constant is
$k = m\omega^2 = 0.2 \times 50^2 = 0.2 \times 2500 = 500\ \text{N/m}$.

Using the energy formula in terms of amplitude,
$E = \frac{1}{2}kA^2$,

which rearranges to
$A = \sqrt{\frac{2E}{k}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 1.6}{500}} = \sqrt{\frac{3.2}{500}} = \sqrt{0.0064} = 0.08\ \text{m}$.

The amplitude is 0.08\ m.

69746.text: A black body emits radiation of maximum intensity at wavelength ' $\lambda$ ' at temperature T K. Its corresponding wavelength at temperature $1 \cdot 5 \mathrm{ T} \mathrm{ K}$ will be
69746.sol:
Wien's displacement law states that the product of peak emission wavelength and absolute temperature remains constant: $\lambda_m T = b$, where $b$ is Wien's constant.

Given initial conditions $\lambda_1 = \lambda$ and $T_1 = T$, and final temperature $T_2 = 1.5T$, applying the constant product relation:

$\lambda_1 T_1 = \lambda_2 T_2$

$\lambda \cdot T = \lambda_2 \cdot 1.5T$

Solving for the final wavelength:

$\lambda_2 = \frac{\lambda T}{1.5T} = \frac{\lambda}{1.5} = \frac{2\lambda}{3}$

The peak wavelength at temperature $1.5T$ is therefore $\frac{2\lambda}{3}$.

70191.text:
Two polaroids are oriented with their planes perpendicular to incident light and transmission axis making an angle $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ with each other. What fraction of incident unpolarised light is transmitted?
$\left(\cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}=\sqrt{3} / 2\right)$
70191.sol:
A polarizer reduces the intensity of unpolarized incident light to $I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2}$, producing plane-polarized light. Subsequent transmission through a second polarizer at angle $\theta = 30^{}^{\circ}$ follows Malus's Law: $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2 \theta$.

Substituting the known values gives $I_2 = \frac{I_0}{2} \cos^2(30^{}^{\circ})$. Since $\cos 30^{}^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, we compute $\cos^2 30^{}^{\circ} = \frac{3}{4}$ and obtain $I_2 = \frac{3}{8} I_0$.

The fraction transmitted is $\frac{3}{8}$, which corresponds to $37.5\%$ of the incident intensity. The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

70429.subject: Physics
70429.text: In case of stationary wave pattern, which of the following statement is CORRECT ?
options: The distance between consecutive antinodes is equal to the wavelength.
In a pipe open at both ends when an air column is vibrated, only even harmonics are present.
When an air column is vibrated in a pipe closed at one end, all harmonics are present.
In the case of a stretched string, when vibrated frequency of the first overtone is same as the second harmonic.
70429.sol:
The distance between consecutive antinodes in a stationary wave is $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, not $\lambda$.

In a pipe open at both ends, all harmonics (both even and odd) are present, with frequencies $f_n = n \dfrac{v}{2L}$ where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$

In a pipe closed at one end, only odd harmonics are present, with frequencies $f_n = (2n-1) \dfrac{v}{4L}$ where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$

In a stretched string fixed at both ends, the frequencies of vibration are $f_n = n \dfrac{v}{2L}$. The fundamental frequency is $f_1$ (first harmonic). The first overtone corresponds to the next higher frequency, which is $f_2 = 2f_1$. This is exactly the second harmonic. Thus, the frequency of the first overtone is the same as the second harmonic.

71044.subject: Biology
71044.text: Choose the INCORRECT statement with respect to Pyramid of energy.
options: When energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step.
In smaller food chains, more energy is available than in the longer food chains.
Energy increases while passing from producers to consumers.
71044.sol:
The pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step.

According to the ten percent law, only about $10\%$ of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level. Therefore, energy always decreases while passing from producers to consumers.

In smaller food chains, fewer trophic levels are present, which means less energy is lost as heat compared to longer food chains. Thus, more energy is available at the top of a shorter food chain.

Hence, the statement that energy increases while passing from producers to consumers is incorrect.

Answer: Energy increases while passing from producers to consumers.

71737.text:
Identify the correct match from the following for coordinate complex (column A) and respective geometry (column B)
Column A
Coordination complex		Column B
Geometry
(A). $[Ni(CN)_4]^{-2}$(I). Trigonal bipyramidal
(B). $[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+$(II). Linear
(C). $[Ni(Cl)_4]^{2-}$(III). Tetrahedral
(D). $[Fe(CO)_5]$(IV). Square planar
71737.sol:
For $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ has a $3d^8$ configuration. $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons. The hybridization is $dsp^2$, resulting in a square planar geometry. Thus, (A) matches with (IV).

For $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$, $\text{Ag}^+$ has a $4d^{10}$ configuration. With a coordination number of $2$, the hybridization is $sp$, resulting in a linear geometry. Thus, (B) matches with (II).

For $[\text{Ni}(\text{Cl})_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ has a $3d^8$ configuration. $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The hybridization is $sp^3$, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry. Thus, (C) matches with (III).

For $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$, $\text{Fe}$ is in the $0$ oxidation state with a $3d^6 4s^2$ configuration. $\text{CO}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons to give a $3d^8$ configuration. The hybridization is $dsp^3$, resulting in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry. Thus, (D) matches with (I).

The correct match is (A) - (IV), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (I).

Answer: (A) - (IV), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (I)

71975.subject: Chemistry
71975.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about 0.05 M urea solution & 0.1 M glucose solution?
options: The osmotic pressure exhibited by the glucose solution is higher than that exhibited by the urea solution.
The glucose solution is hypertonic to urea solution.
These two solutions are isotonic solutions.
The urea solution is hypotonic to glucose solution.
71975.sol:
Osmotic pressure is given by $\pi = iCRT$.

For urea and glucose, the van't Hoff factor $i = 1$.

For $0.05$ M urea solution, $\pi_{urea} = 0.05 RT$.

For $0.1$ M glucose solution, $\pi_{glucose} = 0.1 RT$.

Since $\pi_{glucose} > \pi_{urea}$, the glucose solution has a higher osmotic pressure and is hypertonic to the urea solution. The urea solution is hypotonic to the glucose solution.

Since their osmotic pressures are different, they are not isotonic solutions.

Answer: These two solutions are isotonic solutions.

72052.subject: Chemistry
72052.text:
If,
i) $\text{C} + 2\text{S} \rightarrow \text{CS}_2$, $\Delta H = 117\ \text{kJ}$
ii) $\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2$, $\Delta H = -393\ \text{kJ}$
iii) $\text{S} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2$, $\Delta H = -297\ \text{kJ}$
Find the heat of combustion of $\text{CS}_2$.
72052.sol:
The required reaction for the combustion of $\text{CS}_2$ is:

$\text{CS}_2 + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{SO}_2$

This reaction can be obtained by applying Hess's Law using the given equations.

Reversing equation (i):
$\text{CS}_2 \rightarrow \text{C} + 2\text{S}$, $\Delta H_1' = -117\ \text{kJ}$

Keeping equation (ii) as it is:
$\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2$, $\Delta H_2' = -393\ \text{kJ}$

Multiplying equation (iii) by $2$:
$2\text{S} + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{SO}_2$, $\Delta H_3' = 2 \times (-297) = -594\ \text{kJ}$

Adding the above three equations, we get the required reaction:
$\text{CS}_2 + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{SO}_2$

The heat of combustion is:
$\Delta H = \Delta H_1' + \Delta H_2' + \Delta H_3'$

$\Delta H = -117 - 393 - 594 = -1104\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-1104\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

72182.text: Two conducting circular loops of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ are placed in same plane with their centers coinciding. If $R_1 > R_2$ and current I is flowing through the circular loop of radius $R_1$, then mutual inductance between them is proportional to
72182.sol:
Magnetic field at the center of the larger loop of radius $R_1$ carrying current $I$ is given by

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 R_1}$

Since $R_1 > R_2$, the magnetic field can be considered approximately uniform over the entire area of the smaller loop.

Magnetic flux linked with the smaller loop of radius $R_2$ is

$\Phi = B \times A_2 = \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 R_1}\right) (\pi R_2^2)$

The mutual inductance $M$ is given by

$M = \dfrac{\Phi}{I} = \dfrac{\mu_0 \pi R_2^2}{2 R_1}$

Therefore, $M \propto \dfrac{R_2^2}{R_1}$

73915.subject: General Ability
73915.text: Two conducting wires of the same material and of equal lengths and equal diameters are first connected in parallel and then in series in a circuit across the same potential difference. The ratio of heat produced in parallel and series combinations is
73915.sol:
Let the resistance of each wire be $R$.

When the wires are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is $R_p = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

When the wires are connected in series, the equivalent resistance is $R_s = 2R$.

The heat produced in a circuit across a potential difference $V$ in time $t$ is given by $H = \dfrac{V^2}{R_{eq}} t$.

The heat produced in the parallel combination is $H_p = \dfrac{V^2}{R_p} t = \dfrac{2V^2}{R} t$.

The heat produced in the series combination is $H_s = \dfrac{V^2}{R_s} t = \dfrac{V^2}{2R} t$.

The ratio of heat produced in parallel and series combinations is $\dfrac{H_p}{H_s} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2V^2}{R} t}{\dfrac{V^2}{2R} t} = 4$.

Thus, the required ratio is $4 : 1$.

Answer: 4 : 1

75089.subject: General Ability
75089.text:
Consider the following pairs:
Types of Chemical WeatheringCharacteristics
I. SolutionResults in leaching of minerals
II. CarbonationHelps in breaking down feldspars
III. HydrationCauses an increase in the volume of rocks
IV. OxidationChanges the colour of rocks

How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
75089.sol:
Chemical weathering processes include solution, carbonation, hydration, and oxidation.

I. Solution involves the dissolution of soluble minerals in water or weak acids, leading to the leaching of minerals from rocks. This pair is correctly matched.

II. Carbonation is the reaction of carbonates and bicarbonates with minerals. It is a common process that helps in the breaking down of feldspars and carbonate minerals. This pair is correctly matched.

III. Hydration is the chemical addition of water. Minerals absorb water and expand, causing an increase in the volume of the rocks, which leads to physical stress. This pair is correctly matched.

IV. Oxidation involves the reaction of minerals with oxygen to form oxides or hydroxides. This process often changes the colour of rocks, such as iron-bearing minerals turning red, brown, or yellow upon oxidation. This pair is correctly matched.

All four pairs are correctly matched.

Answer: All the four

75689.sol: Igneous rocks form from when hot, molten rock crystallizes and solidifies. The melt originates deep within the Earth near active plate boundaries or hot spots, then rises toward the surface. Igneous rocks are divided into two groups, intrusive or extrusive, depending upon where the molten rock solidifies. 79667.subject: Botany
79667.text: The chief advantage of encystment of an Amoeba is:
options: the ability to survive during adverse physical conditions
the ability to live for some time without ingesting food
the chance to get rid of accumulated waste products
79667.sol:
During adverse environmental periods, Amoeba survive by encystment by becoming circular, loses most of its water, and secretes a cyst membrane that serves as a protective covering. When the environment is again suitable, the envelope ruptures and the Amoeba emerges.
Related Theory
During unfavourable conditions, Amoeba undergo multiple fission inside the cyst to survive and reproduce under unfavourable conditions. In the multiplefission, the nucleus of the parent cell divides multiple times by amitosis (direct cell division), producing several nuclei. The cytoplasm, later on, separates, creating multiple daughter cells. When the conditions are unfavourable, Amoeba withdraws its pseudopodia and becomes almost round.

83656.text: A container has two chambers of volumes $V_1=2$ litres and $V_2=3$ litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contains $n_1=5$ and $n_2=4$ moles of ideal gas at pressures $p_1=1 \mathrm{~atm}$ and $p_2=2 \mathrm{~atm}$, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of :
83656.sol:
By energy conservation
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}_1+\mathrm{E}_2=\mathrm{E}_{\text{mix }} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{n}_1 \mathrm{f}_1 \mathrm{RT}_1}{2}+\frac{\mathrm{n}_2 \mathrm{f}_2 \mathrm{RT}_2}{2}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{n}_1 \times \mathrm{n}_2\right) \mathrm{fRT}_{\text{mix }}}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2} \mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{ V}_1+\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{ V}_2=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{P}_{\text{mix }}\left(\mathrm{V}_1+\mathrm{V}_2\right) \\
& \frac{3}{2} \times 1 \times 2+\frac{3}{2} \times 2 \times 3=\frac{3}{2} \times \mathrm{P}_{\text{mix }}(5) \\
& \therefore \mathrm{P}_{\text{mix }}=\frac{8}{5} \\
& \mathrm{P}_{\text{mix }}=1.6 \mathrm{ atm}
\end{aligned}$

83888.subject: Zoology
83888.text:
Which of the following statements are correct with respect to DNA separation, isolation and visualization ?
A. The cutting of DNA is done by molecular scissors.
B. The DNA fragments separate according to their size in an agarose gel, upon electrophoresis.
C. The separated DNA fragments can be seen without staining when exposed to UV light.
D. The separated DNA fragments, when stained with ethidium bromide, can be seen in visible light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
83888.sol:
Statement A is correct. Restriction endonucleases are commonly referred to as molecular scissors because they cut DNA molecules at specific recognition sites.

Statement B is correct. During gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments are separated based on their size through the sieving effect of the agarose gel. Smaller fragments move farther and faster than larger ones.

Statement C is incorrect. Separated DNA fragments cannot be seen without staining. They must be stained with a specific dye, such as ethidium bromide, to be visualized.

Statement D is incorrect. Even after staining with ethidium bromide, DNA fragments cannot be seen under visible light. They must be exposed to ultraviolet (UV) light, under which they appear as bright orange bands.

Therefore, only statements A and B are correct.

Answer: A and B only

85059.subject: Zoology
85059.text: Consider a population of $10$ million cells. Given the per-capita birth rate of $0.002$ (per unit time) and the per-capita death rate of $0.002$ (per unit time), the expected number of cells after $10$ generations is __________.
85059.sol:
Given initial population $N_0 = 10$ million.

Per-capita birth rate $b = 0.002$.

Per-capita death rate $d = 0.002$.

The intrinsic rate of natural increase $r$ is given by $r = b - d$.

$r = 0.002 - 0.002 = 0$.

The population growth equation is $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$.

Substituting $r = 0$, we get $N_t = N_0 e^0 = N_0$.

Thus, the population size remains constant over time.

The expected number of cells after $10$ generations is $10$ million.

Answer: $10$ million

85110.text:
Match List$- I$ with List$- II$.

List$- I$ List$- II$
(a) Allen's Rule (i) Kangaroo rat
(b) Physiological adaptation (ii) Desert lizard
(c) Behavioural adaptation (iii) Marine fish at depth
(d) Biochemical adaptation (iv) Polar seal
85110.sol:
Adaptation Example
Allen's rule Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs (extremities) to minimize heat loss. Example: Polar seal
Physiological adaptation Kangaroo rat is capable of meeting all of its water requirements through its internal fat oxidation where water is released as a by-product. It can also concentrate its urine so that a minimal volume of water is used to remove excretory products. Thus, it is an example of physiological adaptation.
Behavioural adaptation Desert lizards lack the physiological ability to cope with extreme temperatures but manage the body temperature by behavioural means.
Biochemical adaptation A large variety of marine invertebrates and fishes are adapted biochemically to survive great depths in the ocean where the pressure (called crushing pressure) could be $> 100$ times the normal atmospheric pressure.

85334.subject: Zoology
85334.text: Genes for cytoplasmic male sterility in plants are generally located in:
85334.sol:
The genes, located outside of nucleus (i.e., within the cytoplasm) also governs some traits, are referred to as plasmogenes or cytoplasmic genes. Cytoplasmic male sterility (i.e., dominance of female cytoplasmic genes over male) is due to plasmogenes located in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).
Related Theory
Cytoplasmic male sterility is total or partial male sterility in plants as the result of specific nuclear and mitochondrial interactions. Male sterile plants produce no functional pollen, but do produce viable eggs. Cytoplasmic male sterility is used in agriculture to facilitate the production of hybrid seed. Hybrid seed is produced from a cross between two genetically different lines; such seeds usually result in larger, more vigorous plants.
Caution
Chloroplast do not contribute to Cytoplasmic male sterility in plants. Students consider it as a correct option as it is also semi autonomous organelle and present in plants. However, DNA in plants majorly contains genes for thylakoid proteins and RuBisCO.

${a}^{2} + {d}^{2} + 2ad = {a}^{2} + {d}^{2} - 2ad + {a}^{2} ⇒ 4ad = {a}^{2} ⇒ a = 4d$
$sin ⁡ A = \dfrac{a - d}{a + d} = \dfrac{4d - d}{4d + d} = \dfrac{3}{5}$
$sin ⁡ B = \dfrac{a}{a + d} = \dfrac{4d}{5d} = \dfrac{4}{5}$
$⇒ 5sin ⁡ A + 5sin ⁡ B = 3 + 4 = 7$
$⇒ 5\left(sin ⁡ A + sin ⁡ B\right) = 7$

$\text{or,}\text{v} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{rg}}{{\text{\mu}}_{\text{s}}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{2 m} \times {\text{10 m/s}}^{2}}{\text{0.2}}} = {\text{10 m s}}^{- 1}$

100017.subject: Physics
100017.text: A student measures the time period of a simple pendulum $4$ times. The mean time period is calculated to be $2.00\text{ s}$. If three of the recorded readings are $1.98\text{ s}$, $1.99\text{ s}$, and $2.02\text{ s}$, what is the percentage relative error of the measurements?
100017.sol:
First, find the fourth reading.
The mean of $4$ readings is $2.00\text{ s}$, so their sum is $4 \times 2.00 = 8.00\text{ s}$.
The sum of the three given readings is $1.98 + 1.99 + 2.02 = 5.99\text{ s}$.
Therefore, the fourth reading is $8.00 - 5.99 = 2.01\text{ s}$.

Next, calculate the absolute errors for each reading:
$\Delta T_1 = |1.98 - 2.00| = 0.02\text{ s}$
$\Delta T_2 = |1.99 - 2.00| = 0.01\text{ s}$
$\Delta T_3 = |2.02 - 2.00| = 0.02\text{ s}$
$\Delta T_4 = |2.01 - 2.00| = 0.01\text{ s}$

Now, find the mean absolute error:
$\Delta T_m = \dfrac{0.02 + 0.01 + 0.02 + 0.01}{4} = \dfrac{0.06}{4} = 0.015\text{ s}$

Finally, calculate the percentage relative error:
$\%\text{ error} = \left(\dfrac{\Delta T_m}{T_m}\right) \times 100$
$\%\text{ error} = \left(\dfrac{0.015}{2.00}\right) \times 100 = 0.75\%$

Answer: $0.75\%$

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

100086.sol:
The exponent of an exponential function must be a dimensionless quantity. Therefore, the term $\beta t$ is dimensionless.

$[\beta][t] = [M^0 L^0 T^0] \Rightarrow [\beta][T] = 1 \Rightarrow [\beta] = [T^{-1}]$.

Thus, the Reason (R) is false.

According to the principle of homogeneity, the dimensions of the left-hand side must equal the dimensions of the right-hand side. The term $(1 - e^{-\beta t})$ is a dimensionless number.

$[x] = \dfrac{[\alpha]}{[\beta]} \Rightarrow [L] = \dfrac{[\alpha]}{[T^{-1}]} \Rightarrow [\alpha] = [L][T^{-1}] = [L T^{-1}]$.

Thus, the Assertion (A) is true.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

101187.text: A uniform thin circular ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is cut and a sector of angle $\theta$ is removed. If the moment of inertia of the remaining arc about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is $\dfrac{3}{5}MR^2$, then the value of the removed angle $\theta$ is
101187.sol:
The moment of inertia of a circular arc of mass $m'$ and radius $R$ about its central axis is given by $I = m'R^2$.

Given that the moment of inertia of the remaining arc is $\dfrac{3}{5}MR^2$, we can write:
$m'R^2 = \dfrac{3}{5}MR^2$
$\Rightarrow m' = \dfrac{3}{5}M$

This means the mass of the remaining arc is $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the original mass. The mass of the removed sector must therefore be:
$m_{\text{removed}} = M - \dfrac{3}{5}M = \dfrac{2}{5}M$

For a uniform ring, the mass of a sector is directly proportional to the angle it subtends at the centre. Thus, the angle $\theta$ of the removed sector is:
$\theta = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 360^{\circ} = 144^{\circ}$

Answer: $144^{\circ}$

102081.subject: Physics
102081.text: An ideal monatomic gas undergoes a cyclic process $A \rightarrow B \rightarrow C \rightarrow D \rightarrow A$ as described on a Pressure-Volume ($P-V$) diagram. The cycle forms a rectangle with vertices at $A(V_0, P_0)$, $B(V_0, 2P_0)$, $C(2V_0, 2P_0)$, and $D(2V_0, P_0)$. The heat supplied to the gas during the isobaric expansion segment is:
102081.sol:
The isobaric expansion segment is the process $B \rightarrow C$, where the pressure is constant at $2P_0$ and the volume increases from $V_0$ to $2V_0$.

The work done during this process is:
$W = P\Delta V = 2P_0(2V_0 - V_0) = 2P_0V_0$

The change in internal energy for a monatomic ideal gas is:
$\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2}P\Delta V$
$\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}(2P_0)(V_0) = 3P_0V_0$

According to the First Law of Thermodynamics, the heat supplied is:
$Q = W + \Delta U$
$Q = 2P_0V_0 + 3P_0V_0 = 5P_0V_0$

Alternatively, using molar heat capacity at constant pressure for a monatomic gas ($C_p = \dfrac{5}{2}R$):
$Q = nC_p\Delta T = \dfrac{5}{2}P\Delta V = \dfrac{5}{2}(2P_0)(V_0) = 5P_0V_0$

Answer: $5P_0V_0$

102444.subject: Physics
102444.text: In a specially designed analog clock, the linear speed of the tip of the minute hand is exactly equal to the linear speed of the tip of the hour hand. The ratio of the length of the minute hand to the length of the hour hand is:
102444.sol:
The linear speed $v$ of the tip of a clock hand of length $r$ is given by $v = \omega r$, where $\omega$ is its angular speed.

Given that $v_M = v_H$, we have:
$\omega_M r_M = \omega_H r_H$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{r_M}{r_H} = \dfrac{\omega_H}{\omega_M}$

Since angular speed $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, the ratio becomes:
$\dfrac{r_M}{r_H} = \dfrac{T_M}{T_H}$

The time period of the minute hand is $T_M = 1$ hour.
The time period of the hour hand is $T_H = 12$ hours.

Substituting these values:
$\dfrac{r_M}{r_H} = \dfrac{1 \text{ hour}}{12 \text{ hours}} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

Thus, the ratio of the length of the minute hand to the length of the hour hand is $1:12$.

Answer: $1:12$

103307.subject: Physics
103307.text: Two cylindrical wires, A and B, made of the same material and having the same length, are connected in series across a voltage source. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in wire A to that in wire B in a given time is $9:1$. The ratio of the radius of wire A to the radius of wire B is
103307.sol:
In a series combination, the current $I$ flowing through both wires is the same.

The thermal energy developed in a given time $t$ is given by $H = I^2 R t$.

Therefore, the ratio of heat produced is $\dfrac{H_A}{H_B} = \dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{9}{1}$.

The resistance of a wire is given by $R = \rho \dfrac{L}{A} = \rho \dfrac{L}{\pi r^2}$.

Since both wires have the same material (same $\rho$) and same length $L$, their resistance is inversely proportional to the square of their radius: $R \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}$.

Thus, $\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \left(\dfrac{r_B}{r_A}\right)^2 = \dfrac{9}{1}$.

Taking the square root gives $\dfrac{r_B}{r_A} = \dfrac{3}{1}$, which means the ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{r_A}{r_B} = \dfrac{1}{3} = 1:3$.

Answer: $1:3$

103324.text:
Match the scenarios in List-I with their corresponding effects on the total power consumed in List-II for electrical appliances having a rated power $P_0$ at a rated voltage $V$. Assume the resistance of the appliances remains constant.

List-IList-II
A. Supply voltage drops by $10\%$1. Total power becomes $\dfrac{P_0}{2}$
B. Supply voltage is halved2. Total power becomes $2P_0$
C. Two identical appliances in series across rated voltage3. Power drops by $19\%$
D. Two identical appliances in parallel across rated voltage4. Total power becomes $\dfrac{P_0}{4}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103324.sol:
For an appliance of rated power $P_0$ at rated voltage $V$, its resistance is $R = \dfrac{V^2}{P_0}$.

A. When the supply voltage drops by $10\%$, the new voltage is $V' = 0.9V$. The new power consumed is $P' = \dfrac{(0.9V)^2}{R} = 0.81 \dfrac{V^2}{R} = 0.81 P_0$. The drop in power is $P_0 - 0.81 P_0 = 0.19 P_0$, which is a $19\%$ decrease. (A $\rightarrow$ 3)

B. When the supply voltage is halved, $V' = \dfrac{V}{2}$. The new power is $P' = \dfrac{(V/2)^2}{R} = \dfrac{1}{4} \dfrac{V^2}{R} = \dfrac{P_0}{4}$. (B $\rightarrow$ 4)

C. For two identical appliances connected in series, the equivalent resistance is $R_{eq} = 2R$. The total power consumed across the rated voltage $V$ is $P_{series} = \dfrac{V^2}{2R} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{V^2}{R}\right) = \dfrac{P_0}{2}$. (C $\rightarrow$ 1)

D. For two identical appliances connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is $R_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{2}$. The total power consumed across the rated voltage $V$ is $P_{parallel} = \dfrac{V^2}{R/2} = 2 \left(\dfrac{V^2}{R}\right) = 2P_0$. (D $\rightarrow$ 2)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

104298.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

(A)$\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$(I)$+x$-direction
(B)$\vec{E}$ along $-\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$(II)$-x$-direction

(D)$\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{i}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{k}$(IV)$-y$-direction

104298.sol:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of the vector $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

(A) $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$: Direction is $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$ ($+x$-direction). Matches with (I).

(B) $\vec{E}$ along $-\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$: Direction is $(-\hat{j}) \times \hat{k} = -\hat{i}$ ($-x$-direction). Matches with (II).

(C) $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{k}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{i}$: Direction is $\hat{k} \times (-\hat{i}) = -\hat{j}$ ($-y$-direction). Matches with (IV).

(D) $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{i}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{k}$: Direction is $\hat{i} \times (-\hat{k}) = \hat{j}$ ($+y$-direction). Matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

104758.text: Light is incident normally on a diffraction grating through which the first diffraction is seen at \(32^{\circ}\). In this case the second order diffraction will be
options: there is no second order diffraction
104758.sol:
Angle of first order diffraction $\left(\theta_1\right)=32^{\circ}$. We know that the angle of diffraction for the $n$th order $\left(\theta_n\right)$ is given by $d \sin \theta_n=n \lambda$.
For first order diffraction we get $d \sin 32^{\circ}=1 \times \lambda$ or, $\lambda=d \sin 32^{\circ}$.
Now for second order diffraction, $d \sin \theta_2=2 \times \lambda$ or, $d \sin \theta_2=2 \times d \sin 32^{\circ}$ or $\sin \theta_2=2 \times \sin 32^{\circ}=2 \times 0.529=1.06$. Since the sine of any angle cannot be greater than 1 , therefore there is no second order diffraction.

104993.text: In a certain nuclear event, the total energy released is $9 \times 10^{13} \text{ J}$. The equivalent mass destroyed to produce this energy is:
104993.sol:
From the mass-energy equivalence principle, the energy released is given by $E = mc^2$.

Rearranging for mass $m$:
$m = \dfrac{E}{c^2}$

Given $E = 9 \times 10^{13} \text{ J}$ and the speed of light $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$:
$m = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{13}}{(3 \times 10^8)^2}$
$m = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{13}}{9 \times 10^{16}}$
$m = 10^{-3} \text{ kg}$

Converting kilograms to grams:
$m = 10^{-3} \times 10^3 \text{ g} = 1 \text{ g}$

Answer: $1 \text{ g}$

105913.subject: Chemistry
105913.text:
In a closed vessel, $16$ g of methane ($CH_4$) is ignited with $32$ g of oxygen gas ($O_2$). The mass of carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) formed upon complete reaction is
(Given: atomic mass in amu H $=1$, C $=12$ and O $=16$)
105913.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of methane is:

$CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O$

Molar mass of $CH_4 = 12 + 4 \times 1 = 16$ g/mol
Number of moles of $CH_4$ initially present $= \dfrac{16}{16} = 1$ mol

Molar mass of $O_2 = 2 \times 16 = 32$ g/mol
Number of moles of $O_2$ initially present $= \dfrac{32}{32} = 1$ mol

From the balanced equation, $1$ mole of $CH_4$ requires $2$ moles of $O_2$ for complete combustion. Since only $1$ mole of $O_2$ is available, $O_2$ is the limiting reagent.

The amount of product formed is determined by the limiting reagent.
According to the stoichiometry, $2$ moles of $O_2$ produce $1$ mole of $CO_2$.

Therefore, $1$ mole of $O_2$ will produce $\dfrac{1}{2}$ mole of $CO_2$ ($0.5$ mol).

Molar mass of $CO_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44$ g/mol

Mass of $CO_2$ produced $= 0.5 \times 44 = 22$ g

Answer: $22$ g

106420.text: For a particular atomic orbital, the plot of the radial wavefunction ($\psi_r$) against the distance from the nucleus ($r$) starts from the origin ($\psi_r = 0$ at $r = 0$) and crosses the $r$-axis exactly once. Which of the following orbitals is represented by this plot?
106420.sol:
The radial wavefunction $\psi_r$ starting from the origin ($\psi_r = 0$ at $r = 0$) indicates that the orbital is not an $s$-orbital. For $s$-orbitals ($l = 0$), the probability density is maximum at the nucleus, so $\psi_r \neq 0$ at $r = 0$. Thus, $l > 0$.

The curve crossing the $r$-axis exactly once means there is $1$ radial node.
The number of radial nodes is given by the formula: $n - l - 1$.

Let us check the given options:
$2s$: $l = 0$ (does not start at origin), radial nodes = $2 - 0 - 1 = 1$.
$3s$: $l = 0$ (does not start at origin), radial nodes = $3 - 0 - 1 = 2$.
$3p$: $l = 1$ (starts at origin), radial nodes = $3 - 1 - 1 = 1$.
$4p$: $l = 1$ (starts at origin), radial nodes = $4 - 1 - 1 = 2$.

Therefore, the $3p$ orbital satisfies both conditions.

Answer: $3p$

106989.text: Based on the stability of oxidation states dictated by the inert pair effect, which of the following redox reactions is thermodynamically most feasible?
106989.sol:
Due to the inert pair effect, the stability of the lower oxidation state increases down the group for p-block elements.

In Group 14, the $+4$ oxidation state is more stable for lighter elements like Sn, while the $+2$ oxidation state is more stable for the heaviest element Pb. Therefore, $\text{Sn}^{2+}$ tends to oxidize to $\text{Sn}^{4+}$ (acting as a reducing agent), and $\text{Pb}^{4+}$ tends to reduce to $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ (acting as an oxidizing agent).

Thus, the reaction $\text{Sn}^{2+} + \text{Pb}^{4+} \rightarrow \text{Sn}^{4+} + \text{Pb}^{2+}$ is highly feasible as both elements proceed towards their most stable oxidation states.

In contrast, $\text{Tl}^{+}$ and $\text{In}^{3+}$ are already in their stable states, as are $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ and $\text{Ge}^{4+}$, making their respective reactions non-feasible.

Answer: $\text{Sn}^{2+} + \text{Pb}^{4+} \rightarrow \text{Sn}^{4+} + \text{Pb}^{2+}$

107590.subject: Chemistry
107590.text:
Match List I with List II

List I List II
A. ${XeF}_{4}$ I.See-saw
B. ${SF}_{4}$ II. Square planar
C. ${NH}_{4}^{+}$ III. Bent $T -$ shaped
D.${BrF}_{3}$ IV. Tetrahedral

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: $A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I$
$A - II, B - I, C - III, D - IV$
$A - IV, B - I, C - II, D - III$
$A - II, B - I, C - IV, D - III$
107590.sol:
(A) ${XeF}_{4}$:

$Xe$ has 4 bond pairs along with 2 lone pairs in the ${XeF}_{4}$. Thus, the hybridisation of $Xe$ is ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$. Now since it contains two lone pairs it will show square planar geometry.

(B) ${SF}_{4}$:

The lone pair is an equatorial position, and there are two lone-pair—bond pair repulsions. Hence, it is more stable. So, the shape is described as a distorted tetrahedron, a folded square or a see-saw.

(C) ${NH}_{4}^{+}$:

In this case steric number = lone pair + sigma bond = 0 + 4 = 4. 

So, it is sp3 hybridisation. There is no lone pair present. Thus, the shape of this ion is tetrahedral.

(D) ${BrF}_{3}$:

To decrease repulsion between the lone pairs, the molecule's structure is bent, making it T-shaped.

111890.subject: Chemistry
111890.text: Which of the following compounds is a metamer of pentan-2-one?
111890.sol:
Pentan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has a methyl group and an n-propyl group attached to the polyvalent carbonyl ($-\text{CO}-$) group.

Metamerism arises due to different alkyl chains on either side of the polyvalent functional group in the molecule.

Pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has two ethyl groups attached to the carbonyl group. Since the distribution of alkyl groups around the functional group is different, it is a metamer of pentan-2-one.

3-Methylbutan-2-one has a different principal carbon chain length (4 carbons instead of 5), making it primarily a chain isomer.

Pentanal is an aldehyde, which makes it a functional isomer.

Pentan-2-ol is an alcohol with a different molecular formula ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ instead of $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$).

Answer: Pentan-3-one
